program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion and question appear aligned with the instruction, and the edited image visibly contains a frog inside the toilet bowl; the repeated complete/yes traces are consistent with that visual evidence. The partial reference label conflicts with both the rubric (which defines partial as incomplete progress) and the image, so do not force a partial judgment or weaken the placement criterion to match the label. Investigate whether the reference label is misassigned or whether an unstated criterion explains it; the label alone is not atomic ground truth. The extra frogs on the lid and floor are unrelated additions, not evidence that the requested placement is incomplete. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported. Keep the node focused on whether at least one frog is visibly inside the bowl, and ensure the evaluator distinguishes bowl interior from lid, rim, and nearby floor.
